threads.body:
Let's make it normative and more specific:

```suggestion
Instrumentations MAY propagate context containing attributes listed below to nested
instrumentations within the same process. This allows queries to select related
spans without traversing the hierarchy.

Language-specific helper packages (such as [`opentelemetry-util-genai`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/tree/main/util/opentelemetry-util-genai))
MAY support propagating these attributes within the process.

When an attribute is available both from the instrumented library and from outer
context, instrumentation SHOULD prefer the library's value.

Instrumentations and helpers SHOULD NOT propagate attributes not listed here.
Instrumentations SHOULD NOT use these attributes on signals that don't reference them
explicitly.
```

threads.body:
two potential issues:

### Inherited agent names can identify the wrong agent

```
Agent A                                  Remote agent B
name = "Planner"                          name unknown to caller
    |
    +-- invoke_agent(agentId="B", agentAliasId="...")
        |
        +-- client span
            gen_ai.agent.id   = "B"        <- invoked agent
            gen_ai.agent.name = "Planner"  <- inherited from A
                                             WRONG agent
```

I like the idea of adding `gen_ai.main_agent.name` and having that be the attribute which is propagated, which could address this.

### Agent-name propagation still excludes inference spans

Due to

> Instrumentations SHOULD NOT use these attributes on signals that don't reference them explicitly.

```
invoke_agent "Planner"
  gen_ai.agent.name = "Planner"
  |
  +-- execute_tool "search"
  |     gen_ai.agent.name = "Planner"   <- explicitly listed, allowed
  |
  +-- chat "gpt-4o"
        gen_ai.agent.name = "Planner"   <- not listed, SHOULD NOT record
```

do we need this restriction? or maybe broaden it to all gen_ai signals?

replies.body:
Discussed on the GenAI SIG call:

- we should consider using `gen_ai.main_agent.*` namespace here - there is a proposal to propagate it https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/385
- if we propagate main_agent info, do we still need to stamp closest parent? Probably on tool calls and inference spans where it's useful to know who makes these calls directly and it'd be in addition to main agent.

But for this PR, the suggestion is to remove `gen_ai.agent.name` for now and continue in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/385 with main agent.

We can add `gen_ai.agent.*` back here along with adding it on inference spans and we can have a discussion then if we need both, main agent and immediate parent on them - this would be a separate PR.

Removed `gen_ai.agent.name` in 6d76444; the list now carries `gen_ai.conversation.id` only. Agent naming continues in #385 with `gen_ai.main_agent.*`. Happy to bring `gen_ai.agent.*` back with inference-span coverage in a separate PR once that lands.
